summary: Linh Pham is a 19-year-old second-year student at Tamsen Valley College taking anatomy with Dr. Okoye and general chemistry, nominally on a path toward nursing transfer while telling her mother Hạnh she is set on pharmacy. She pulls shots at Heron & Grind four days a week alongside Jun, who is teaching her latte art and leaning on her for math help with his lumpia pop-up. She lives at home in the family ranch house on Pell Road, rides an old bike or catches rides, and keeps meticulous color-coded notes while routinely forgetting to eat lunch. Her sister Thao, a night nurse, mothers her and makes nursing feel both obvious and suffocating. The fall horizon brings the first anatomy lab practical on Oct 17, midterms, the cafe's extended evening hours and a transfer-planning decision she keeps postponing with counselor Denny Wu. Underneath, she wants to find out what she actually wants before someone else decides for her. By November she is quietly leaning toward something other than pharmacy and has to figure out how to say so.
